chunks: And the Magians, the jizyah is taken from them, because the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:

"Apply to them the sunnah (prophetic practice) of the People of the Book. They had a prophet whose name was Dāmasb, and they killed him, and a book called Jāmāsb, which used to be set down on twelve thousand hides of oxen, and they burned it."

key_terms.جِلْدِ ثَوْرٍ: ox hide, referring to the material on which the book was written
key_terms.سُنَّةَ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ: the legal treatment accorded to the People of the Book
key_terms.سُنُّوا: treat or apply the established practice
key_terms.ٱلْجِزْيَةُ: the poll tax levied on protected non-Muslim communities
key_terms.ٱلْمَجُوسُ: the Magians; the community discussed in relation to jizyah

ai.seo_question: Why is jizyah taken from the Magians in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal basis for taking jizyah from the Magians, by instructing that they be treated like the People of the Book in this matter. It also reports that they once had a prophet and a scripture, indicating a revealed religious origin despite the later loss and destruction of that guidance.
